info.name: MyFlix API (authenticated)
info.description: All 7 MyFlix tables with real logins. Set the collection variable publishable_key (your sb_publishable_... key), then Run the collection in order. Folder 0 signs up (or reuses) two test accounts and saves their access tokens; every table request sends user A's token, and folder 8 uses user B's token to prove RLS isolation. Needs 'Confirm email' OFF in Supabase (Authentication > Sign In / Providers > Email). Cleans up its rows at the end.

item.name: 0 Auth

request.description: Creates test user A (name goes into the auth metadata; the database trigger copies it into public.users). 422 means the account already exists from an earlier run, which is fine.

item.name: Sign in user A (saves access_token, user_id)
Sign in user B (saves access_token_b, user_id_b)

item.description: Sign up (or reuse) two test accounts and sign both in. Every request after this sends a user's access token.

item.name: GET genres with a filter (name = Action)
GET titles with a filter (type = show, name = Echo Drift)
GET titles in the user's genres (Action + Sci-Fi)
GET the title with its genre names
GET user B's row by id -> empty
PATCH my email -> 403 (only name is editable)
POST a user -> 403 (the sign-up trigger creates rows)
GET Continue watching (unfinished, with title info)
Upsert (what the app sends): POST with on_conflict

exec: // The upsert also needs Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates

item.name: 8 Isolation: user B vs user A's rows
B: GET favorites -> doesn't see A's
B: GET in_progress -> doesn't see A's
B: PATCH A's in_progress -> 0 rows changed
B: DELETE A's favorite -> 0 rows deleted
B: POST a favorite as user A -> 403 (RLS with check)
A: still has the favorite and S2E6

item.description: Proves RLS: B can't read, change, delete, or create A's rows, and logged-out requests get nothing.

item.name: POST favorite for a title that doesn't exist -> 409
POST in_progress with a blank left_off -> 400
10 Cleanup
item.description: Removes the rows this run created and signs both users out. The two test accounts stay in Authentication > Users (the publishable key can't delete accounts); delete them there if you want a clean list.
